blocks.content: Start with an existing SQL data source and a populated table containing a time field and two categorical fields.
Open **SQL Drilldown** to explore a table without writing SQL.
blocks.tooltip: Start with the databases available in your Grafana instance.

blocks.content: You are ready to choose which table to investigate.
Choose a table, focus its rows, and compare its column distributions.

Choose a supported data source, then select its project and dataset or database when those scope controls appear. Make these choices yourself because the names come from your data; wait for the table list to load.
blocks.tooltip: Choose the source and scope containing the records you want to investigate.

blocks.content: Choose **Browse table** on a populated table with a time column and two categorical columns, such as service and region. Select your own table, then wait for **Rows** to display its records.
blocks.tooltip: Open a populated table whose time and category fields you want to explore.

blocks.content: Choose the time field in **Time column** yourself, using a column whose timestamps overlap the current time range. Confirm that matching records remain visible.
blocks.tooltip: Align the records with the time range you are investigating.

blocks.content: Use **Columns** to keep the time field and the categorical fields you want to compare, then close the picker. Choose the actual fields from your table so the visible records contain useful context.
blocks.tooltip: Keep the fields that will help you recognize a pattern in the records.

blocks.content: Choose a modest **Limit**, such as 100, from the available choices and confirm that the table refreshes. Make the selection yourself to keep this first investigation manageable.
blocks.tooltip: Bound the result set while you learn what each record contains.

blocks.content: Open **Breakdown** to compare how the records are distributed across column values.
blocks.tooltip: Compare the distribution of values in the same table.

blocks.content: You have bounded the rows and moved to the same table’s column breakdowns.
Compare a column’s values, group them by another field, and keep one group to inspect its records.
Choose a categorical field from the **Columns** sidebar yourself and inspect its individual values. Use a field present in your table, then wait for its value charts to appear.
blocks.tooltip: Pick a category whose individual values could explain the pattern you saw.

blocks.content: Choose another categorical field in **Group by** yourself, then compare the resulting groups. For example, a service grouped by region can help reveal where its records are concentrated.
blocks.tooltip: Split each value into another useful dimension from the same table.

blocks.content: Choose **Include** on one visible value group that has records, then confirm that its filters appear. Choose the value yourself because it comes from your data; do not click an already included value again, which would remove the filter.
blocks.tooltip: Keep one value group and check that the filter is applied.

blocks.content: Return to **Rows** to inspect the records behind the value group you selected.
blocks.tooltip: Return to the individual records while retaining the filters.

blocks.content: Read the matching records and confirm that the value and group filters are still applied. You should see the chosen table with your selected columns and limit, now narrowed to the group you investigated rather than an error or empty result.
blocks.tooltip: Confirm that the visible records match the group you kept.

blocks.content: You have explored a column breakdown and returned to matching rows with the value and group filters still applied.
